2O.11 Sing songs in thanks to God for all His goodness and the wonderful works He has done.

points: The work of the house of the Most High was finished, and Solomon brought in all that David his father had dedicated, the silver, the gold, and the instruments, and laid them among the treasures of the house.
The temple did not begin from nothing. What the father set apart, the son carried into its place. The dedicated things of one generation are stored up for the work of the next.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel, the heads of the tribes, and the chiefs of the fathers to bring up the ark of the covenant out of the city of David, which is Zion.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: All the men of Israel gathered at the feast in the seventh month. The dedication was tied to the appointed time, not to a date of convenience.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: The Levites took up the ark, the tabernacle of the congregation, and all the holy vessels, and the priests and Levites brought them up.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: Solomon and all the congregation before the ark sacrificed sheep and oxen that could not be numbered for multitude. This was a celebration, a gathered nation of Israel in order, in beautiful garments, keeping the appointed feast together.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: The priests brought the ark into the oracle of the house, into the most holy place, under the wings of the cherubims, whose wings covered the ark and the staves above it.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: The staves were drawn out so their ends could be seen from before the oracle but not from without. The video shown in class pictured this same scene, the two great cherubims flanking the ark with wings stretched from wall to wall.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: There was nothing in the ark except the two tables Moses put there at Horeb, where the Most High made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt.
The ark held the covenant, the written law. The center of the most holy place pointed back to the commandments given at the exodus.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: When the priests came out of the holy place, the Levite singers, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun with their sons and brethren, stood arrayed in white linen with cymbals, psalteries, and harps, and a hundred and twenty priests sounded with trumpets.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: The trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound in praising and thanking the Most High, saying He is good, for His mercy endureth for ever. This was order, everything set in unison, the whole assembly on one accord.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 5: The Ark Brought Into the House and the Glory That Filled It

points: When the one sound of praise went up, the house was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud.
The glory of the Most High had filled the house. The cloud was His glory settling upon the temple, His answer to a people gathered in order and in praise.
